correctness.rationale: Binary joint probabilities reduce exactly to three Laplace transforms. Finite-exponential uniqueness recovers named rate lists and diagonal sum multiset. Two-class alternatives have a nonzero squared-sum difference under distinct positive rates, and explicit three-class associations share all three multisets but differ as paired sets. A finite forbidden ratio set is sufficient for all candidate off-diagonal exponent sums to be distinct, proving full matching recovery for any finite number of classes. The embedded exact-rational verifier checks the explicit witness and a finite two-class grid; the unrestricted steps are proved analytically, not inferred from code. No field or finite-sample assertion is made.

value.rationale: The mathematical object is naturally motivated by joint host/parasite presence–absence assays with effort scaling. The counterexample invalidates inference of within-class host–parasite shedding association from an entire common-effort curve, not merely a finite-sample approximation; sharp minimal class count and a one-extra-ratio design show exactly what structural information is and is not recoverable. This is a meaningful inverse-design boundary despite stringent idealizations; no field calibration is claimed.
